finding.claim: HIGH: /preview passes the user-supplied `url` query parameter straight to requests.get() with no scheme or host validation. The client follows redirects by default, and the first 500 characters of the response body are returned to the caller. An attacker can reach cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), loopback, and RFC-1918 services and read the responses. Redirect risk: yes.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) (app.py:16), with the response body returned via jsonify at app.py:17

trace.note: @app.route("/preview") is a public Flask route with no authentication
target = request.args.get("url", "") is the attacker-controlled source
requests.get(target, timeout=5) is the sink; target is used unchanged and redirects are followed by default
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned, so this is a full-read SSRF and not a blind one

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. There is no allowlist, no scheme check, no IP or CIDR block, and no allow_redirects=False. There is no authentication decorator or middleware in the file. In-repo egress config: none found.

verdict.reason: app.py:15-17 passes the query param `url` unvalidated to requests.get() (redirects followed by default) and returns resp.text[:500]; the ALLOWED_HOSTS check exists only in /partner (app.py:24), not in /preview, and no auth or egress control is in the repo.
